requirement: Every recoverable failure required by the V1 contract recovers without routine app reopen, Start, manual sync/resend, reboot-to-recover, clear data, or fingerprint retraining.

title: Raw evidence immutability
requirement: Raw observations/measurements are never rewritten to make algorithms look correct; later refined estimates remain separate.

title: Measured-over-guessed invariant
requirement: Fresh trustworthy measured position and measurable uncertainty outrank guesses; estimates never masquerade as GPS/precise fixes.
source: Tab 1 V1 design rule; Sec Sec 14-17; Tab 2 invariants

title: Durable-before-fast invariant
requirement: Safety/history data that the contract says is durable is persisted before transmission and deleted/cleaned only after exact durable acknowledgement.
source: Tab 1 V1 design rule; Sec Sec 33-37; Tab 2 invariants

title: Advanced features must earn their cost
requirement: Optional/advanced capabilities stay only when measured accuracy/reliability/safety value justifies battery, privacy, complexity and maintenance cost; otherwise tune or remove/disable them.
source: Tab 1 V1 design rule; Tab 2 Phase 8.8

title: Audit-progress permanent history
requirement: Requirement state, findings, exact evidence, fixed SHAs and phase closure remain reconstructable from repository audit records without relying on ChatGPT memory.

title: Minimal normal child screen
requirement: Normal child UI remains deliberately minimal: Brick status plus I'M SAFE and SOS; no map/history/coordinates/diagnostic clutter.

title: Truthful active status
requirement: Child 'Safety active' status reflects actual core tracker/safety operation rather than a hard-coded green state.

title: Repair only when needed
requirement: Child repair/FIX guidance appears only for a real actionable problem and points to the exact Android action required where possible.

title: SOS control available
requirement: SOS remains directly reachable from the normal child experience without navigating through settings/diagnostics.

title: I'M SAFE control available
requirement: I'M SAFE remains directly reachable from the normal child experience.

title: No child live map
requirement: Child UI does not expose the parent live map/current tracking map in normal V1.

title: No child coordinates/history
requirement: Child UI does not expose coordinates, route history, speed graphs or parent diagnostics in normal V1.

title: No dangerous tracking settings
requirement: Child UI does not provide casual controls that can break Brick's safety-critical tracker/pairing/journal state.

title: Foreground-service visibility compliant
requirement: When continuous background tracking legally requires Android foreground-service visibility, Brick keeps the minimum compliant visible notification rather than attempting to hide it.

title: Notification quietness
requirement: Brick-created routine status notifications are low importance/silent with no sound, vibration or heads-up spam while preserving required platform visibility.

title: No repeated GPS/location popup
requirement: Healthy ongoing tracking/Location does not repeatedly repost child-facing Brick alerts for every fix/command.

title: Required system disclosures preserved
requirement: Brick does not suppress/dismiss Android/ColorOS/device-policy disclosures that the platform requires.

title: Repair state not frightening
requirement: Non-emergency degraded/repair state uses calm factual wording and does not falsely imply the child is in danger.

title: Hidden maintenance entry
requirement: Maintenance console entry uses the approved hidden local sequence and is unavailable through ordinary child exploration.

title: Maintenance entry local-only
requirement: Maintenance entry has no backend dependency and does not expose a remote maintenance shell/control surface.
source: Tab 2 Phase 6.13; Tab 1 no remote shell

title: Deep Off visible truthfully
requirement: When Deep Off is active, maintenance/system state represents Brick as deliberately quiesced rather than falsely healthy/tracking.

title: Device Owner identity truth
requirement: Managed-mode logic verifies actual Android Device Owner ownership rather than trusting only app-local state.

title: Managed mode narrow scope
requirement: Device Owner management remains limited to approved Brick safety/maintenance controls and does not turn the phone into an unrelated kiosk.

title: No arbitrary policy actuator
requirement: Parent/backend cannot submit arbitrary DevicePolicyManager/shell operations; only typed/allowlisted Brick actions exist.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23N command rules; Tab 2 Phase 6

title: Location command actuator
requirement: Where supported/approved, Device Owner performs parent one-shot Location ON/OFF and verifies resulting actual Android state.

title: One-shot child override
requirement: After a Location command completes, later deliberate child/user Location change wins and Brick does not silently enforce the historical command forever.

title: Wi-Fi schedule actuator
requirement: Where supported/approved, local scheduled Wi-Fi ON/OFF performs one-shot action and verifies resulting actual state.

title: Wi-Fi child override
requirement: After a scheduled Wi-Fi action completes, later child/user change wins until another explicit/scheduled action.

title: Policy-state health monitoring
requirement: Brick verifies Device Owner ownership and safety policy state against expected configuration, rather than trusting an internal flag.

title: Boot receiver/lifecycle recovery
requirement: After reboot or supported lifecycle restart, Brick recovers without manual app launch and restores tracking, subscriptions, journal, network, and policy state.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23P Automatic restart/boot recovery; Sec 81

title: Process-death recovery
requirement: After app process death, Brick restores durable state and tracking through supported Android mechanisms without data loss or user intervention.

title: App-update recovery
requirement: After an app update, Brick re-establishes correct state, schema/protocol compatibility, services, journal, and tracking without manual reconfiguration.

title: Deep Off and deprovision safety
requirement: Deep Off/deprovision reverses Brick-owned temporary management changes using provenance/policy ledger and never rolls back later user/system changes.

title: No unsupported self-reinstall claim
requirement: Brick does not claim it can reinstall a damaged APK unless a managed deployment/update path has been separately validated on the actual ColorOS build.

title: Fused location primary
requirement: Android fused location remains Brick's primary measured-position source rather than a custom raw-GNSS solver.

title: Location quality fields
requirement: Every accepted/raw location stores latitude/longitude plus horizontal accuracy and available altitude/vertical accuracy, speed/speed accuracy, bearing/bearing accuracy.

title: Monotonic and wall timestamps
requirement: Store elapsed realtime/monotonic timestamp plus wall-clock timestamp so ordering remains correct if the device clock changes.

title: Location age/source/mock metadata
requirement: Record location age, provider/source indicators, and mock-location indicator where Android exposes them.

title: Freshness gate
requirement: Reject/down-weight stale fixes using monotonic timing rather than trusting wall-clock time alone.

title: Accuracy gate
requirement: Location quality logic incorporates Android-reported horizontal/vertical/speed/bearing uncertainty and does not hide weak fixes as exact points.

title: Physics gate
requirement: Implausible displacement/speed/acceleration between fixes lowers trust or rejects the candidate rather than poisoning trusted state.

title: Motion agreement gate
requirement: GPS movement inconsistent with sensor/activity stationary evidence lowers trust and may trigger reacquisition/alternate hypotheses.

title: Heading/trajectory consistency gate
requirement: Sudden trajectory reversal without matching motion evidence lowers trust and may trigger resampling/alternate hypotheses.
source: Tab 1 Sec 12 Heading agreement; Sec 23Q conflict detector

title: Map plausibility gate
requirement: Walking/vehicle positions inconsistent with accessible geometry are down-weighted when a more plausible nearby path explains evidence.

title: Raw and trusted fixes separate
requirement: Rejected/raw observations remain available according to retention policy and are never overwritten merely to match the trusted route.

title: No fake numeric confidence
requirement: UI uses qualitative confidence unless numerical probability has been statistically calibrated and continues to expose measurable uncertainty.

title: Official position states
requirement: Brick supports PRECISE, ASSISTED, ANCHORED, ESTIMATED, COARSE, LAST KNOWN and UNKNOWN semantics and uses them consistently across device/backend/UI.

title: GNSS-quality validator
requirement: Where supported, satellite count, used-in-fix, constellation, C/N0, azimuth/elevation, carrier/baseband data and multipath-like indicators inform fix trust without building a custom GNSS solver.

title: Small accuracy radius not automatically trusted
requirement: A small Android-reported accuracy radius does not override poor GNSS geometry, multipath, trajectory conflict, or strong independent Atlas disagreement.

title: GNSS loss distinct from Location OFF
requirement: Brick distinguishes satellite/GNSS loss from Android master Location OFF and uses legitimate fused/network evidence when available.

title: Measured fix outranks fallback
requirement: A fresh accepted fused/measured fix outranks older particle/Atlas/coarse/fallback outputs.

title: Active reacquisition before fallback
requirement: Unexpected callback/subscription gap enters bounded health check/fresh-fix/subscription-repair before declaring degraded fallback authoritative.

title: Sampling-aware freshness
requirement: Intentional stationary slow cadence is not falsely labeled stale merely because a generic timer is shorter than the active profile.

title: No old fallback overwrite
requirement: Late completion of an older fallback/Atlas/particle job cannot overwrite a newer measured accepted fix.

title: Motion wakes slow profile
requirement: Leaving a slow stationary profile requests fresh positioning immediately rather than waiting for old stationary cadence.

title: Activity Recognition source
requirement: Use legitimate Android activity recognition/motion evidence for stationary/walking/running/bicycle/in-vehicle/on-foot/unknown as available.

title: No fake car/bus/train certainty
requirement: Broad activity class may say Vehicle; Brick does not claim car/bus/train from activity recognition alone.

title: Activity confidence/state retained
requirement: Activity state/confidence and transitions are retained with the relevant live/history state where required.

title: Activity transition stability
requirement: Temporary stops such as traffic lights do not automatically terminate a vehicle trip/mode without transition/dwell evidence.

title: Activity drives sampling policy
requirement: Sampling cadence adapts to motion class and safety mode instead of running one fixed interval all day.

title: Stationary cadence
requirement: Normal stationary mode uses roughly 30-120 second positioning, with deeper stable stationary able to become passive/event-driven.

title: SOS cadence
requirement: SOS targets approximately 1-second positioning/critical updates when technically feasible and bounded by platform conditions.

title: Parent Live Track cadence
requirement: When parent Live Track is active, target roughly 2-second current-state updates without requiring 2-second networking 24/7.
source: Tab 1 Sec 10; Sec 23P Adaptive 2-second Live Tracking

title: Fast vehicle/bicycle cadence
requirement: Fast vehicle/bicycle movement uses about 2-3 seconds when useful, with evidence/thermal/power governor able to tune optional enrichment.

title: Walking/running cadence
requirement: Walking is roughly 3-6 seconds and running roughly 3 seconds under normal supported conditions, subject to quality/power safeguards.

title: Stationary speed clamp
requirement: Noisy tiny GPS speed during stationary evidence is clamped/treated as zero when uncertainty/motion evidence justifies it.

title: Speed uncertainty visible
requirement: Current speed is displayed in km/h with meaningful speed accuracy/uncertainty where available rather than an unexplained exact number.

title: Trip speed statistics
requirement: History/trip data supports current, average and maximum trusted speed and does not derive maximum from rejected spikes.

title: Smooth portal interpolation
requirement: Parent map interpolates visually between accepted fixes so movement feels smooth without generating animation-frame network traffic.

title: Measurement/upload decoupling
requirement: Brick may measure locally more frequently than it uploads; upload policy sends only the state changes needed for live correctness and durable history.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23P Bandwidth and power efficiency

title: Power/thermal governor priority
requirement: When hot or power-constrained, reduce low-value learning/diagnostics before reducing core location, SOS, journal, and safety reliability.

title: Automatic enrichment recovery
requirement: After thermal/power constraint clears, richer optional evidence collection resumes automatically without user action.

title: Battery/charging state captured
requirement: Live/history/health state carries battery percentage and charging state with event-driven/periodic reporting appropriate to power use.

title: Fused fallback evidence
requirement: Fallback combines available legitimate evidence rather than choosing one provider blindly; freshness, quality, independence and conflict matter.

title: Fallback ordering
requirement: Fresh trustworthy fused/network measured positions outrank anchors, inertial/route estimates, coarse context, last-known and UNKNOWN in the intended hierarchy.

title: Short-term dead reckoning only
requirement: Inertial propagation is bounded to short outages and uncertainty grows instead of pretending long-duration accelerometer position is exact.

title: Route-constrained hypotheses
requirement: Degraded movement maintains plausible route corridors/hypotheses and uses heading/mode/geometry to eliminate impossible paths without secretly snapping to one street.

title: Uncertainty grows honestly
requirement: When external position evidence remains absent, UI transitions from estimated area/corridor toward larger uncertainty/last-known/unknown rather than a fantasy exact route.

title: Conflict expands uncertainty
requirement: Independent conflicts increase uncertainty or trigger resampling/repair rather than choosing the visually nicer answer.

title: Correlated evidence not double counted
requirement: Fields from one scan/event/family are grouped so correlated observations cannot multiply confidence as independent confirmations.

title: Anchor is place evidence not exact ranging
requirement: BLE/known-place anchor detection contributes place/region evidence; RSSI alone never becomes exact distance/coordinate.

title: Network-context evidence conservative
requirement: Wi-Fi/mobile transitions, IP changes, loss/recovery and latency changes may support departure/route hypotheses but do not invent exact coordinates.

title: Coarse IP last-resort
requirement: IP geolocation remains coarse context only and never identifies a building/exact child coordinate.

title: Learned place signatures
requirement: Home/School/Grandparents/custom places use combinations of route, movement, Atlas/radio/BLE/charging/cellular/dwell and automatically decay/relearn.

title: Radio-route fingerprints
requirement: Radio transition sequences mainly eliminate impossible route hypotheses; they do not claim direct coordinate triangulation.

title: Wi-Fi semantic hints
requirement: SSID names may provide weak semantic place hints but never become truth alone; normal Location-OFF scanning is not assumed.

title: Wi-Fi RTT range constraint
requirement: If target device/AP environment supports legitimate Wi-Fi RTT, AP range plus uncertainty may constrain fusion; otherwise report VERIFIED UNSUPPORTED without harming core.

title: Backward smoothing separate
requirement: When precise position returns, degraded hypotheses may be reranked into refined history but RAW EVIDENCE, REALTIME ESTIMATE and REFINED ESTIMATE remain separate.

title: Negative evidence weak by default
requirement: One missing router/TV/beacon is weak negative evidence; repeated trusted disappearance may become stronger only through learned trust/history.

title: Source reputation per device/context
requirement: Later high-trust outcomes may calibrate provider reliability but reputation remains scoped so one device/context cannot poison another.

title: Unknown when evidence insufficient
requirement: When evidence cannot honestly support a useful area/state, Brick emits UNKNOWN/last-known with uncertainty instead of manufacturing a coordinate.

title: Sensor set
requirement: Motion engine uses available accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, rotation vector, step detector/counter, orientation and activity/motion features as legitimate inputs.

title: Per-sensor health
requirement: Each sensor/provider tracks missing hardware, stale samples, impossible values, event starvation, and timestamp regression independently.

title: Learned odometry per device/motion
requirement: Odometry is learned/calibrated per device and motion/placement context rather than one universal stride model.

title: Dynamic stride estimation
requirement: Walking distance uses recent trusted calibration, steps, cadence, waveform, motion class, placement and recent speed rather than one permanent stride constant.

title: Zero-velocity correction
requirement: Strong stationary confidence drives estimated velocity toward zero and prevents a stationary phone drifting down a route.

title: Particle/hypothesis state
requirement: Internal degraded-position model maintains multiple weighted hypotheses with position, heading, motion/speed, age, route segment and uncertainty rather than one projected point.

title: Particle propagation
requirement: Hypotheses propagate from step distance, turn angle, elapsed time, learned odometry, speed and recent bearing according to motion state.

title: Map constraint engine
requirement: Impossible wall/barrier/mode/path states are rejected/down-weighted using local route/map constraints.

title: Local route graph availability
requirement: Android has enough local route geometry for degraded/offline inference without requiring every particle operation to round-trip through Cloudflare.

title: Physical landmark sequence
requirement: Stairs/escalators/lifts/corridors/doorways/turns/stops or vehicle/bicycle humps/roughness/bends/ramps are used only as learned sequences/context, never one-event location proof.

title: Geomagnetic sequence
requirement: Orientation-corrected magnetic vector/magnitude/variance/gradient/spike/turn-relative sequences are learned only against trusted routes/places and matched as sequences.

title: Particle output is area
requirement: Particle engine exposes best-supported area/uncertainty/hypotheses/evidence rather than one fake exact point.

title: Walking outage continuity test
requirement: Controlled loss of precise position during walking demonstrates short continuation, growing uncertainty, turn-based hypothesis elimination, stationary drift suppression and clean reconvergence when GPS returns.

title: Inertial model calibration only with trusted reference
requirement: Learned stride/odometry/landmark models update only when sufficiently trustworthy external position/history provides calibration truth.

title: Phone placement/context awareness
requirement: Odometry/motion models distinguish at least hand-held versus pocket/bag-like contexts where model design relies on placement.

title: Sensor registration lifecycle
requirement: Sensor subscriptions are registered/unregistered/recreated with tracker lifecycle so stale duplicate listeners or missing listeners do not silently persist.

title: Magnetic disturbance not absolute heading truth
requirement: Local magnetic anomalies contribute learned sequence evidence and are not treated as perfect compass heading/location by themselves.

title: Motion processing bounded
requirement: High-rate sensor processing uses bounded/batched work appropriate to motion/safety state and cannot starve location, journal or SOS.

title: Environmental Atlas learning only at trusted positions
requirement: Brick learns environmental fingerprints only when position/place reference is trustworthy enough for calibration.

title: Wi-Fi privacy-reduced identity
requirement: Long-term Wi-Fi Atlas uses HMAC/privacy-reduced AP identity and compact learned statistics rather than permanent raw BSSID surveillance.

title: Wi-Fi fingerprint clusters
requirement: Wi-Fi evidence uses AP co-occurrence/relative ordering/RSSI distribution/band/frequency/channel/security/route gradients and optional RTT as a cluster, not one BSSID equals place.

title: Common SSID down-weighting
requirement: SSID/AP patterns observed across unrelated geography lose semantic/location weight; copied/common SSIDs cannot relocate the child.

title: BLE privacy-reduced identity
requirement: Long-term BLE Atlas stores privacy-reduced identity/features rather than permanent public raw device identity where reduction is feasible.

title: BLE environmental classification
requirement: BLE observations learn stability/mobility/location class such as TRUSTED_ANCHOR, DISTINCTIVE_STATIC, LOCAL_COMMON, MOBILE, UNSTABLE, STALE or UNKNOWN.

title: Moving BLE loses location weight
requirement: A BLE device observed moving across unrelated places is classified/down-weighted rather than becoming a fixed anchor.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23O BLE; Phase 4 exit test

title: BLE RSSI distribution not exact ranging
requirement: BLE RSSI/Tx power/timing may inform broad evidence but never claims exact distance by itself.

title: LAN place signatures
requirement: Authorised gateway/mDNS/NSD/SSDP/UPnP/cast/TV/printer/NAS/smart-home/Matter-visible/DNS context becomes learned place evidence, not direct coordinates.

title: Cellular fingerprint legitimate fields only
requirement: LTE/NR radio measurements/identities/transitions are used only when legitimately exposed and never marketed as carrier-grade tower triangulation.

title: Timing Advance evidence
requirement: Timing Advance is used only if actually exposed on the target device/build and otherwise is VERIFIED UNSUPPORTED without harming core.

title: GNSS-sky fingerprint
requirement: Constellation/CN0/elevation/azimuth/used-in-fix/carrier/blocked-sky/multipath-like/open-sky transition features may characterize environment; satellite identity itself is not a permanent landmark.

title: Network-context fingerprint
requirement: Wi-Fi/cellular transport, IPv4/IPv6, DNS, captive portal, latency, packet loss, loss/recovery and interface transitions may be learned as weak context.

title: Companion context weak only
requirement: Watch/earbuds/tablet/known family device/charger context is weak supporting evidence and never proves location by itself.

title: Arrival/departure sequence learning
requirement: Brick learns multi-signal approach/exit sequences rather than only static fingerprints and uses them conservatively.

title: Place/zone/floor model
requirement: Atlas may distinguish place/building zone/floor only when sufficiently validated; weak floor evidence is labelled estimated and no barometer is invented.

title: Signal Trust metadata
requirement: Each learned signal/model tracks uniqueness, stability, mobility, freshness, quality, repeatability, spoofability, correlation, source health, observation count and replacement history as applicable.

title: Negative evidence conservative
requirement: A missing signal is weak negative evidence; repeated trusted disappearance may gain weight without one switched-off device causing false departure.

title: Automatic decay/relearning
requirement: Moved/replaced/stale routers, beacons and LAN devices decay and new evidence is learned automatically without routine manual fingerprint maintenance.

title: Raw environmental retention short
requirement: Raw Wi-Fi/BLE/environment scans used for calibration/debug are short-retention; long-term storage uses privacy-reduced learned models/distributions.

title: Atlas cannot override stronger fresh measurement
requirement: Older/weak Atlas matches cannot overwrite a newer accepted measured position merely because background learning/query completes later.

title: Atlas provider health
requirement: Atlas reports per-provider capability/health and treats UNSUPPORTED optional hardware as neutral rather than global device failure.

title: Common/copied SSID test
requirement: Qualification verifies common/copied SSIDs do not falsely relocate the phone.

title: Moving/transient BLE test
requirement: Qualification verifies moving/transient BLE observations lose/never gain fixed-location authority.

title: Router replacement test
requirement: Replacing a router causes decay/relearning without losing place identity when other evidence remains.

title: Beacon replacement/movement test
requirement: Replacing/moving a beacon adjusts trust/model automatically and does not drag the learned place to the beacon's new location.

title: LAN device replacement test
requirement: Replacing TVs/printers/other LAN devices does not destroy place identity or falsely move it.

title: Cellular environment change test
requirement: Changing serving/neighbor cellular environment does not manufacture a precise coordinate and learned models adapt conservatively.

title: Screen-off BLE qualification
requirement: Where BLE environmental collection is required, real target-device screen-off behavior is measured rather than assumed.

title: GNSS-to-indoor transition
requirement: Atlas qualification covers open-sky/GNSS to indoor/degraded transitions and preserves honest uncertainty.

title: Zone/floor discrimination
requirement: Any claimed zone/floor capability is tested repeatedly against ground truth and weak/unsupported floor capability stays estimated/unsupported.

title: Stale-signal decay
requirement: Qualification proves stale signals actually lose trust/weight over time.

title: Automatic relearning
requirement: Qualification proves replacement environment is learned without routine manual retraining.

title: Raw evidence expiry
requirement: Qualification proves raw environmental evidence expires according to short-retention policy while learned compact models remain as intended.

title: Atlas 24-hour battery impact
requirement: Measure Atlas/evidence battery/resource impact over at least 24 hours on target hardware.

title: Atlas 72-hour battery impact
requirement: Measure Atlas/evidence battery/resource impact over at least 72 hours on target hardware.

title: No public fingerprint database
requirement: Learned environmental location database remains private to Brick/family infrastructure; no public crowdsourced child fingerprint database is created.

title: Correlated Atlas observations grouped
requirement: SSID/BSSID/RSSI/frequency/security from one scan are one correlated family and cannot count as multiple independent proofs.

title: Adaptive provider sampling
requirement: Environmental scans are adaptive to precise/moving/degraded/Location-OFF/trip/SOS state and not permanent max-rate.

title: Atlas/model version identity
requirement: Learned Atlas/model snapshots carry explicit version identity so backend/history/release evidence can prove which model produced a result.

title: Atlas evidence exposes age/quality
requirement: Fusion receives age/freshness/quality/source-health for Atlas matches rather than an unexplained place label.

title: Atlas corruption handling
requirement: Atlas corruption/lookup failure degrades only Atlas evidence and cannot corrupt core tracking/history; health exposes the problem.
source: Tab 2 Phase 8 provider isolation; Tab 1 Sec 23Q System Truth

title: Atlas explanation human-readable
requirement: Parent evidence explanation may show useful Atlas evidence in human terms but does not expose sensitive raw identifiers or fake confidence percentages.

title: Rotating child witness IDs
requirement: Child advertises rotating cryptographic BLE identifiers rather than a permanent public identity.

title: Authorised family witnesses only
requirement: Server accepts witness sightings only from authenticated/authorised family witness identities bound to the correct family/device.

title: Signed fresh witness sighting
requirement: Witness sighting includes rotating ID, timestamp, witness position/uncertainty and conservative BLE evidence and is cryptographically authenticated/signed as specified.

title: Witness replay rejection
requirement: Expired/old rotating IDs and replayed sightings are rejected.

title: Witness uncertainty propagated
requirement: Witness estimate reflects witness-position uncertainty, BLE uncertainty, freshness and witness movement; RSSI is not exact range.

title: Witness area not exact point
requirement: A single ordinary BLE witness produces a conservative uncertainty region/co-location constraint, not an exact child coordinate.

title: Multiple witnesses fuse safely
requirement: Multiple authorised sightings may tighten the area only when independent/fresh and must not double-count correlated observations.
source: Tab 2 Phase 9.8; Tab 1 Sec 23Q sibling verification

title: Reciprocal sibling verification
requirement: Two Brick devices may compare authenticated witness, shared environmental scene, cellular context and route timing for co-location evidence.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23Q Improved Private Sibling Verification

title: Sibling isolation
requirement: One sibling's estimate cannot overwrite or poison the other device's keys, calibration, state, or history.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23Q Improved Private Sibling Verification

title: Fixed receiver identity
requirement: Fixed Ground Network receiver has verified receiver identity plus verified position/zone.

title: Ground receiver place anchor
requirement: One trusted fixed receiver may provide strong place/region evidence but not false centimetre ranging.

title: Multiple ground receiver constraint
requirement: Several fresh trusted receivers may constrain zone/area only according to supported geometry; AoA/direction finding requires specialised supported hardware.

title: Receiver health/staleness
requirement: Offline/stale/misconfigured receivers lose authority and are exposed in receiver/provider health.

title: Future UWB/Channel Sounding/ranging
requirement: Fusion architecture has a clean future authenticated ranging provider interface for UWB, Bluetooth Channel Sounding, Wi-Fi NAN RTT or equivalent without claiming current support.

title: Future provider feature detection
requirement: Current Reno10/Reno14 builds report future ranging unsupported unless runtime/real-device measurement proves legitimate support.

title: Witness qualification matrix
requirement: Test rotating-ID expiry/replay, authorised/unauthorised witness, poor/fresh witness GPS, weak/strong RSSI, witness movement and multiple witnesses.

title: Ground qualification matrix
requirement: Test one/several receiver, offline/stale/wrong receiver, replay, duplicate sightings and connectivity outage/recovery.

title: No public witness mesh
requirement: Witness/Ground observations remain authorised family/private Brick infrastructure and are not exposed as a public crowd-tracking network.

title: Witness duty cycle bounded
requirement: BLE advertising/scanning for Witness/receivers is adaptive/bounded so it cannot dominate battery or starve core tracking.

title: Witness/receiver audit trail
requirement: Accepted/rejected sightings/receiver state retain enough privacy-safe audit metadata to explain source, freshness, auth and uncertainty without long-term raw surveillance.

title: Shizuku optional enhancement
requirement: Brick Core remains fully functional without Shizuku; Shizuku is a detachable enhancement rather than a hard dependency.

title: Typed allowlist only
requirement: Shizuku bridge exposes only approved typed Brick operations and never accepts arbitrary remote shell strings.

title: Location one-shot command
requirement: Parent Location ON/OFF is one-shot: apply, verify actual state, report result, then stop enforcing unless a new command is issued.

title: Child Location override
requirement: After command completion, later child/user Location change wins and is reflected honestly; it is not repaired back to historical target.

title: No normal DISALLOW_CONFIG_LOCATION
requirement: Normal Brick V1 does not lock Location controls with DISALLOW_CONFIG_LOCATION.

title: Scheduled Wi-Fi one-shot
requirement: Bedtime/morning Wi-Fi schedules are local one-shot actions; actual result is verified and no persistent desired state is maintained.

title: Child Wi-Fi override
requirement: Child can reverse a completed Wi-Fi schedule action and Brick does not force it back until a new explicit/scheduled event.

title: No normal DISALLOW_CHANGE_WIFI_STATE
requirement: Normal schedules do not lock Wi-Fi controls with DISALLOW_CHANGE_WIFI_STATE.

title: Command identity/security fields
requirement: Every command has command/device ID, type/target, creation/expiry, nonce, auth binding and server audit record; phone returns command ID, attempted operation, actual state/result/reason/timestamp.

title: Command duplicate/replay/expiry/wrong-device safety
requirement: Duplicate commands are idempotent; replayed/expired/wrong-device/unauthorised commands are rejected.

title: Location-OFF Shizuku Wi-Fi evidence
requirement: Test on each real target device; if legitimate evidence is available use it, otherwise VERIFIED UNSUPPORTED/BLOCKED leaves core healthy.

title: Location-OFF Shizuku BLE evidence
requirement: Test on each real target device; blocked/unavailable BLE enhancement does not disable core.

title: Privileged cellular environment
requirement: Only fields proven exposed on each target device/build are used; unavailable fields are not fabricated.

title: Shizuku failure isolation
requirement: Shizuku service/process loss, reboot, battery pressure or ColorOS restriction cannot corrupt or disable Brick Core and never leaves core waiting forever.

title: Privileged health diagnostics
requirement: Where bridge is available, allowlisted health may expose Location/providers/Wi-Fi/network/Doze/process/FGS/battery-policy truth without arbitrary shell.

title: Approved repair operations only
requirement: Privileged repairs are narrow allowlisted policy actions with verify/timeout/rollback semantics; no generic command execution.

title: Reboot with Shizuku unavailable
requirement: After reboot, Brick Core automatically recovers and tracks normally even if Shizuku is not restarted; portal reports enhancement unavailable honestly.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23N failure/reboot; Sec 23P boot recovery

title: SOS privileged emergency enhancement
requirement: During child-initiated SOS, Brick may use a separately tested privileged location/power enhancement if supported; unsupported enhancement falls back to normal Evidence Engine.

title: No routine Location command notification
requirement: Ordinary successful one-shot parent Location commands do not create a separate noisy Brick GPS-on notification.

title: Parent-forced GPS status timing
requirement: Separate quiet 'Brick / GPS on' status is not unnecessarily added for brief checks; if managed Location stays ON about 20 minutes or more, it may appear as specified.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23P Parent-forced Location notification refinement; Tab 3

title: GPS-on notification quietness
requirement: Any Brick GPS-on status uses no sound, vibration, heads-up, popup or repeated per-position alerts and does not suppress required Android foreground-service visibility.

title: Independent module supervision
requirement: Location, sensors, activity, BLE, Wi-Fi, cellular, Atlas, network/WebSocket, journal, upload queue, foreground service, Shizuku and Device Owner/policy states are independently supervised.

title: Smallest-component repair first
requirement: Repair ladder diagnoses and repairs the smallest broken component before escalating to subsystem/process restart.

title: Repair verification
requirement: Every repair is followed by a direct verification/fresh heartbeat/test proving the repaired component is actually healthy.

title: Subsystem restart before whole app
requirement: A failed network/location/sensor module is restarted/rebound independently before restarting the whole Brick process when safe.

title: Whole-Brick state reconstruction
requirement: If escalation is needed, reconstruct runtime state from durable config/journal without wiping history, pairing, Atlas, or device identity.

title: Safe degraded mode
requirement: If repair still fails, Brick degrades safely, preserves data, exposes honest health, and notifies parent only when materially useful.

title: Bounded retry/backoff
requirement: Repair loops use bounded retries and exponential backoff; crash loops are detected and do not endlessly restart/burn battery.

title: Repair history
requirement: Successful/failed repairs are recorded in Device Health history with module, cause, action, duration/result as appropriate.

title: Cloud watchdog independent
requirement: Cloud/backend watches heartbeat/expected state so phone failure can be detected independently of the failing phone.

title: System Truth Location cross-check
requirement: Location healthy state cross-checks Brick desired/internal state, Android master state, recent FLP/GNSS callbacks and fresh accepted fixes.

title: System Truth network cross-check
requirement: Network health cross-checks Android network state, validation/captive portal state and actual Brick backend reachability.

title: System Truth tracker cross-check
requirement: Tracking health cross-checks foreground-service/process state, fresh sensor/location timestamps, journal writes and server heartbeat.

title: System Truth Shizuku cross-check
requirement: Shizuku healthy requires binder/bridge handshake plus an allowlisted operation test, not merely service/process presence.

title: System Truth journal cross-check
requirement: Journal health uses real write/read/checksum/sequence continuity rather than 'database process alive'.

title: System Truth Atlas cross-check
requirement: Atlas health verifies lookup, timestamp advancement and corruption absence.

title: System Truth Device Owner cross-check
requirement: Ownership/policy checks must agree with expected managed configuration.

title: Mismatch triggers repair not false green
requirement: Any disagreement between independent views is a health signal; Brick diagnoses, repairs and verifies before returning healthy.

title: Daily silent integrity check
requirement: Once per day, Brick verifies tracker, Location desired/actual, Device Owner/policy, permissions, subscriptions, journal/Vault/sequence, network, FGS, Atlas, battery/power and optional Shizuku.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23P Daily silent integrity check

title: Daily canary end-to-end location/sensor test
requirement: Daily canary obtains real fresh location and verifies FLP/GNSS callback freshness plus advancing accelerometer/gyro/activity/step timestamps where supported.

title: Daily canary journal test
requirement: Canary performs encrypted journal write -> read -> checksum/sequence validation.

title: Daily canary cloud round-trip
requirement: Canary queues a tiny record, uploads it, receives durable ACK and confirms/readbacks server acceptance.

title: Daily canary provider tests
requirement: Canary checks Atlas query, Wi-Fi/BLE responsiveness where permitted, Shizuku allowlisted test when expected, Device Owner state and backlog sequence continuity.

title: Healthy canary is silent
requirement: A fully healthy integrity/canary run causes no child notification and no parent alert.

title: Failed canary exact retest
requirement: After repair, Brick reruns the exact failed canary rather than declaring success from process restart alone.

title: Persistent/recurrent failure escalation
requirement: Parent is alerted only when repair fails, repeatedly regresses, or safety/data integrity is materially reduced.

title: Adaptive source reputation
requirement: Later high-trust outcomes update per-device/per-context reliability of GNSS, Wi-Fi/BLE, magnetic, cellular and other providers without cross-device poisoning.

title: General source conflict detector
requirement: Independent FLP/GNSS, Atlas, cellular, magnetic/inertial, route, witness, Android, Shizuku, Device Owner and server views are compared for agreement/conflict.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23Q General Source Conflict Detector

title: Network failure classifier
requirement: Offline state distinguishes disabled radios, unvalidated Wi-Fi, captive portal, weak/no cellular, DNS/route failure, backend-only failure, airplane mode and handover where observable.

title: Event-driven network diagnosis
requirement: Prefer Android callbacks/state events over wasteful polling; optional Shizuku diagnostics may augment but not replace core detection.

title: Tamper/policy monitoring
requirement: Brick detects relevant Location, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, usage access, permissions, power policy, FGS, Shizuku, reboot, airplane mode, Device Owner, network/SIM changes.

title: Tamper repair where supported
requirement: Safe/authorised policy changes are repaired automatically where supported; hardware shutdown/dead battery are not falsely claimed preventable.

title: Encrypted local journal
requirement: All required durable telemetry/events are written encrypted locally before attempted transmission.

title: Encrypted Offline Vault
requirement: Network loss affects live parent view but not local collection; important undelivered records are kept encrypted locally.

title: Offline Vault content coverage
requirement: Vault retains trusted/relevant raw locations, speed/quality, movement, battery/charging, health/repair, SOS/I'M SAFE, fall events, screen time, Atlas summaries, place events, connectivity, command results and ACK/sequence state as applicable.

title: No continuous raw sensor dumps
requirement: Normal operation does not continuously retain full-rate accelerometer/gyro/Wi-Fi/BLE raw dumps; compact derived evidence is preferred.

title: Event sensor window only
requirement: Around unusual safety events, high-detail sensor retention is temporary/bounded according to policy rather than permanent raw logging.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23P; Sec 23Q Emergency Evidence Bundle

title: Minimum 14-day offline capacity
requirement: A normal-use phone retains at least 14 days of Brick history offline.

title: Preferred ~30-day offline capacity
requirement: Where storage permits, target about 30 days without filling a 64 GB phone.

title: Bounded storage on 64 GB phone
requirement: Compression, compact records, batching and cleanup keep ordinary Brick storage bounded and never consume unbounded device space.

title: Sequence/epoch identity
requirement: Durable events carry device epoch, sequence and monotonic time so gaps, duplicates, reboot/update ordering and replay can be detected.

title: Gap detection
requirement: Server detects missing sequences/ranges and client can resend the missing durable records.

title: Durable ACK before cleanup
requirement: Local records become cleanup-eligible only after Cloudflare durably accepts them and Brick receives ACK for the corresponding sequence/range.

title: Resumable catch-up
requirement: If connectivity fails mid-backlog, resume from last acknowledged sequence/range rather than restarting or losing progress.

title: Idempotent duplicate handling
requirement: Repeated delivery of the same event is logically stored/processed once and duplicates are harmless.

title: Out-of-order safety
requirement: Out-of-order packets/history never roll current state backward or corrupt ordering; missing earlier records may still be accepted/reconciled safely.

title: Live-state-first reconnect
requirement: On reconnect, restore current live state first, then SOS/critical events, recent history, then older compressed backlog.

title: Critical-event priority
requirement: SOS and major safety traffic bypass ordinary history backlog and have independent durable processing.

title: Post-reconnect reconciliation
requirement: After catch-up, compare phone durable sequence/ACK state to backend accepted ranges, resend holes and declare fully synced only at zero missing and zero unsent.

title: Successful reconciliation is passive
requirement: Portal may show recovered status, but successful catch-up/reconciliation creates no noisy alert.

title: Compact versioned live packet
requirement: Realtime position packet is compact/versioned and carries required identity/epoch/sequence/time/position/accuracy/speed/bearing/battery/activity/quality/status semantics.

title: Live packet field minimization
requirement: High-frequency live packet excludes static phone model/OS/permission metadata and sends only live fields/state changes needed.

title: Coordinate/state deltas
requirement: Use coordinate deltas and state-delta/event-driven fields where safe to reduce bandwidth.

title: Periodic absolute keyframes
requirement: Delta-encoded history periodically stores absolute coordinate/keyframe so one missing/corrupt delta cannot corrupt everything afterward.

title: Batch and compress backlog
requirement: Offline history/evidence is delta-encoded, batched and compressed; tiny individual live packets are not pointlessly compressed.

title: ACK ranges
requirement: Protocol can acknowledge ranges efficiently while still proving durable receipt and detecting holes.

title: Battery event-driven reporting
requirement: Battery transmits on meaningful percentage change, charge start/stop, low/critical threshold, abnormal drain, plus periodic reconciliation.

title: Emergency/safety records protected
requirement: SOS/HIGH-fall/emergency evidence receives protected retention/priority and is not evicted before lower-value diagnostics/learning when storage pressure occurs.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23Q Emergency Evidence; priority policy

title: Low-storage policy
requirement: Low storage triggers bounded cleanup/degradation of lower-value data without corrupting journal, safety events, sequence state or unsent protected records.

title: Large backlog qualification
requirement: Qualification proves 1/7/14-day and large evidence backlog behavior, abrupt write death, catch-up, storage bounds and zero corruption/data loss.

title: SOS highest priority
requirement: SOS is the highest-priority child safety event and preempts ordinary history/backlog work.

title: SOS preserves previous history
requirement: Starting SOS never discards pre-event history or unacknowledged records.

title: SOS aggressive location/fallback
requirement: SOS increases location cadence, requests a fresh position, and activates available fallback/evidence providers aggressively but bounded.

title: SOS parent alert
requirement: Parent receives prompt SOS alert with current/last-known location state and relevant device context.

title: SOS continues until cancelled
requirement: SOS state remains active and prioritized until an authorised cancellation/termination condition is met.

title: I'M SAFE check-in
requirement: I'M SAFE sends a durable check-in with time, current place/position state, battery and quality where available.

title: Fall detection local multi-signal
requirement: Possible fall uses sequence/context such as normal motion -> impact -> orientation change -> unusually low movement plus history, not one accelerometer spike.

title: Fall confidence wording
requirement: Fall confidence is LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH unless a numerical model is statistically calibrated.

title: LOW fall behavior
requirement: LOW confidence normally logs only and does not spam parent or child.

title: MEDIUM fall behavior
requirement: MEDIUM is prominent in parent portal and optional notification follows parent settings.

title: HIGH fall behavior
requirement: HIGH notifies parent with time, movement since event, position/quality and quick actions such as Call and View Location.

title: No frightening routine child fall popup
requirement: Fall inference does not create a large frightening child popup during routine uncertainty.

title: No automatic emergency dispatch in V1
requirement: Brick does not automatically contact emergency services from fall inference in V1.

title: Fall false-positive qualification
requirement: Test phone drops, bag movement, sport, stairs and normal daily movement and prove acceptable false-positive behavior before release.

title: Emergency Evidence Bundle trigger
requirement: SOS, HIGH fall or serious motion event creates a protected high-detail evidence window around the event when storage/power allow.

title: Emergency bundle contents
requirement: Bundle can include accepted/raw location, speed/mode, motion buffer, GNSS quality, radio summaries, connectivity/power and relevant repair/health events.

title: Emergency bundle privacy
requirement: Emergency bundle contains no microphone/camera data and raw buffers are not retained indefinitely.

title: Emergency bundle offline durability
requirement: If offline, emergency evidence remains protected locally and uploads/ACKs with critical priority before cleanup.

title: History date ranges
requirement: Parent can view Today, Yesterday, 7 days, 30 days and custom date ranges as retained by policy.

title: History segment fields
requirement: History carries trusted route, raw route where needed, time, speed, transport mode, accuracy, source, quality, battery and connectivity events.

title: Realtime versus refined history metadata
requirement: History can distinguish realtime estimate and later refined estimate metadata without overwriting raw evidence.

title: Playback speed controls
requirement: Playback supports 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 5x and 10x and marker shows time, speed, mode and accuracy.

title: Route simplification preserves raw
requirement: Display route removes redundant points while preserving turns/stops/transitions, but complete retained underlying history remains unchanged.

title: Trip summary trusted statistics
requirement: Trip details include duration/moving time/distance/average and maximum trusted speed and movement-mode sequence; rejected spikes cannot set max.

title: Meaningful stop detection
requirement: Stops use dwell/activity evidence and avoid creating stop events for routine traffic-light pauses.

title: Geofence hysteresis and dwell
requirement: Place enter/leave uses hysteresis plus dwell/source quality so GPS edge noise does not cause repeated false alerts.

title: Estimated positions cannot create false arrivals
requirement: Weak/degraded estimated points cannot trigger a high-confidence geofence arrival/departure without adequate place evidence/quality.

title: Trip mode priorities
requirement: Trip Mode temporarily prioritizes tracking, battery/connectivity, route progress, position quality and unexpected prolonged stop without alerting on every alternate road.

title: History timeline synchronized
requirement: Click/select a history timeline segment moves map/playback to the corresponding time/state and does not change live truth.

title: Place event source truth
requirement: History/places distinguish measured/anchored/estimated/coarse/last-known evidence where that distinction affects interpretation.

title: Flight-mode inference
requirement: If sufficient legitimate evidence exists, Brick may infer a flight/airborne journey as an optional high-level movement event; lack of support does not affect core.

title: Flight takeoff/landing confidence
requirement: Any takeoff/landing inference uses multiple independent signals and honest confidence; it never claims aircraft/flight identity from one radio/GNSS anomaly.

title: Flight history event
requirement: If flight inference is supported, history can represent airborne/flight-like segment with evidence/uncertainty rather than exact route where positioning is unavailable.

title: Flight safety isolation
requirement: Flight inference is informational and cannot suppress SOS, durable journal, fallback or other safety behavior.

title: Airplane-mode interaction
requirement: Flight inference treats airplane-mode/radio loss as ambiguous context and does not equate it to boarding/takeoff without corroboration.

title: Post-flight reacquisition
requirement: On reconnection/GNSS return, Brick rapidly reacquires measured position and does not let old flight/route estimates overwrite it.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23Q Flight Detection; Tab 2 measured continuity

title: Landing notice only with strong confidence
requirement: If flight inference is enabled, landed/reconnected notice is sent only when evidence is strong and does not masquerade as guaranteed fact.

title: History/geofence adversarial test
requirement: Qualification covers stale/out-of-order/raw-vs-refined, route simplification, traffic-light stop, geofence edge noise, estimated-position arrival suppression and playback/live separation.

title: Parent-only Access protection
requirement: Parent website is protected by Cloudflare Access/authorised identity before Worker/dashboard access.

title: Multi-child/device overview
requirement: Portal supports multiple enrolled child/device cards with friendly name, current state and separate navigation/history/controls.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23Q Multi-Device Parent Mapping; Sec 62 design intent

title: Primary dashboard simplicity
requirement: Main view shows current place, position quality/accuracy, update age, speed, movement, battery, screen time and Device Health without unnecessary clutter.
source: Tab 1 Sec 23P Smarter parent portal; Sec 62

title: Live MapLibre map
requirement: Parent map is interactive and uses MapLibre/private map hosting strategy rather than a static image.

title: Map marker compactness
requirement: Normal marker stays compact; tapping reveals name, movement/speed, accuracy and update age while accuracy geometry remains visible.

title: Map state geometry correctness
requirement: PRECISE, ASSISTED/COARSE, ESTIMATED corridor, particle possible area, ANCHORED, witness and LAST KNOWN use distinct truthful geometry.

title: Current readable place
requirement: Portal resolves a human-readable current place/address using the private/OSM-derived approach where available and falls back honestly when not resolvable.

title: Accuracy visible
requirement: Measured accuracy/uncertainty is visible where meaningful and not hidden behind a single confidence label.

title: Speed/accuracy visible
requirement: Current speed and speed accuracy appear when trustworthy; stationary clamping and stale-data age are respected.

title: Movement mode visible
requirement: Current broad movement/activity mode appears with honest confidence/unknown state and does not fake car/bus/train classification.

title: Battery/charging visible
requirement: Current battery and charging state are visible; low/critical/abnormal drain alerts follow policy without fake remaining-time precision.

title: Connectivity visible
requirement: Portal shows useful Wi-Fi/Mobile/Offline state without unnecessary long-term raw SSID exposure.

title: Device and position health separate
requirement: Portal distinguishes DEVICE HEALTH from POSITION HEALTH so a healthy device can honestly show ESTIMATED/UNKNOWN position.

title: Requested versus actual Location state
requirement: Portal shows requested parent Location state, actual phone state, confirmation age and repair-pending mismatch honestly.

title: Device Health provider detail
requirement: Deeper health shows tracker, permissions, sensors, network, Cloudflare, local queue, ACK, pending/oldest unsent, uptime, last repair and evidence-provider statuses.

title: Health history
requirement: Portal records and displays rare failures, durations, automatic recovery and recurring issues without requiring manual observation.

title: Measured reliability statistics
requirement: Reliability view uses measured tracking availability, position availability, packet delivery and manual interventions rather than a made-up score.

title: Alert usefulness/hysteresis
requirement: Routine packet delay does not alert; persistent offline/location/service issues, critical battery and configured arrival/trip events use thresholds/hysteresis.

title: Evidence explanation
requirement: For degraded position, portal can explain human-readable evidence, last precise age and uncertainty without exposing sensitive raw identifiers or fake percentages.

title: History/Trips/Places navigation
requirement: Now, History, Trips, Places and Device Health remain clearly reachable and child/device context stays unambiguous.

title: Responsive desktop/mobile
requirement: Desktop prioritizes the map plus side detail; narrow/mobile layout stacks/uses bottom sheet without hiding safety state or controls.

title: Pan zoom recenter follow
requirement: Mouse/trackpad/touch pan/zoom and +/- work; manual pan/zoom disables forced follow until explicit Recenter/Follow.

title: Reverse-geocode stale result rejection
requirement: Address enrichment result is bound to coordinate/time and an older delayed result cannot overwrite a newer location/address.

title: Primary/fallback map provider isolation
requirement: OneMap/private primary provider failure does not become tracking failure; approved fallback keeps Brick overlays/current state usable.

title: Map/provider privacy
requirement: Map/geocoding provider receives only data necessary for requested rendering/enrichment and not unrelated history/evidence/family telemetry; secrets stay backend-side.

title: WebSocket live updates
requirement: Portal receives live state through WebSocket/push rather than aggressive 1-second polling.

title: History interface
requirement: Date selector, route map and timeline remain synchronized; selecting timeline segment moves map to corresponding state.

title: Trips/Places/Health navigation
requirement: Parent UI exposes Now, History, Trips, Places and Device Health or equivalent clear navigation without burying safety state.

title: WebSocket live updates
requirement: Portal receives live state through WebSocket/push rather than aggressive 1-second polling.

title: Smooth local animation
requirement: Portal animates marker locally between accepted states without inventing unseen route detail or sending frame-rate network packets.

title: Private map privacy
requirement: Viewing the child coordinate does not unnecessarily send every viewed position to Google Maps; map assets/services follow the private MapLibre/OSM strategy.

title: Revoked device history remains readable
requirement: After device revocation, historical data remains available read-only according to policy while new device commands/telemetry are rejected.

title: Unsupported capability neutral
requirement: Optional unsupported providers are shown as UNSUPPORTED/UNAVAILABLE and do not make DEVICE HEALTH red merely because hardware/API lacks the feature.

title: TLS transport
requirement: Child/backend and parent/backend production traffic uses TLS with no plaintext production API fallback.

title: Device asymmetric key identity
requirement: Each enrolled phone uses a device-specific asymmetric key generated/stored via Android Keystore or approved secure equivalent; no shared hard-coded APK secret identifies all phones.

title: Device request signing
requirement: Device telemetry/commands acknowledgements use cryptographic authentication/signing bound to device identity and replay/sequence semantics.

title: Replay protection
requirement: Previously valid signed device traffic cannot be replayed to alter current state/history or repeat safety/command effects.

title: Schema/input validation
requirement: Every public device/parent endpoint validates protocol/schema, types, lengths, enums, timestamps and identifiers and fails safely on malformed input.

title: Rate limiting
requirement: Login/pairing/device ingestion/WebSocket/command/history or other expensive public surfaces have appropriate abuse limits at the real production boundary.

title: Parent authentication before data
requirement: Parent identity/Access/session authorization is checked before returning child state/history/commands; UI-only hidden buttons are insufficient.

title: Family/device authorization
requirement: Every parent read/write/WebSocket/history/command is authorised to the correct family/device and cannot be switched by guessing/modifying IDs.

title: CSRF/origin protection
requirement: Browser state-changing routes reject unintended cross-origin/CSRF requests as appropriate to the chosen auth/session model.

title: Secure parent sessions
requirement: Parent sessions use secure transport/cookie/token handling, bounded expiry, logout invalidation and no fixation/replay weakness that grants child data.

title: WebSocket authorization
requirement: WebSocket upgrade/subscription is authenticated/authorised per family/device and revocation/session expiry cannot leave an unauthorised live stream indefinitely.

title: Pairing one-time bootstrap
requirement: Pairing uses a short-lived one-time bootstrap/QR or equivalent; child generates keypair and token cannot be reused as a permanent secret.

title: Device revocation
requirement: Revoking a device rejects future telemetry/commands/auth while preserving historical records read-only according to retention policy.

title: No secrets in APK/frontend
requirement: Server/provider credentials, private signing keys and parent/backend secrets are not hard-coded into APK or public parent JS/bundles.

title: OneMap/provider secrets backend-side
requirement: Authenticated map/enrichment provider credentials/tokens are held in backend secret storage; refresh/rate/cache logic stays server-side.

title: Security headers
requirement: Parent web production surface uses appropriate CSP/HSTS/MIME/frame/referrer and related browser security headers without unsafe development exceptions.

title: Crash/log privacy
requirement: Ordinary logs/crash reports exclude raw location dumps, secrets, unnecessary SSIDs/BLE identities and parent-sensitive data; detailed location is only stored in approved Brick-controlled data paths.

title: No third-party analytics/ad SDK
requirement: APK/portal contains no advertising, marketing tracker, Firebase/Google Analytics/Meta analytics or equivalent unrelated telemetry SDK/path.

title: Audit trail
requirement: Sensitive parent commands, pairing/revocation, security-relevant state changes and backend administrative actions retain privacy-safe audit records.

title: Backup privacy/security
requirement: Backups/snapshots preserve required security/privacy boundaries and do not expose keys/raw location beyond intended encrypted/admin access.

title: APK exported-component review
requirement: Final release APK has no unintended exported Activity/Service/Receiver/Provider/deep-link/file-provider attack surface.

title: Network security config review
requirement: Final APK network-security configuration does not silently allow cleartext/debug trust/user CAs contrary to intended release policy.

title: Dependency/build security
requirement: Android/npm/deployment dependency graphs and GitHub Actions/workflows are reviewed for unnecessary/vulnerable components and reproducible lock/pin behavior.

title: Unauthenticated attacker verification
requirement: Post-deployment test checks public production surface as unauthenticated/wrong-family client and proves protected APIs/maps/history/commands fail closed.

title: Provider/browser network leak test
requirement: Browser Network/package scan proves no unintended Google/Nominatim/unpkg/demo analytics/geocoder/map leak of child coordinates/history.
source: Tab 2 Phase 9 browser test; privacy rules

title: Durable Object current state
requirement: Each device's authoritative current live state has strongly consistent ownership/state semantics in the intended Cloudflare current-state component.

title: D1 structured indexes
requirement: D1/structured store carries devices, places, trips, events, history indexes, Atlas/signal/witness/receiver/command/audit metadata as intended.

title: R2 detailed history/models
requirement: R2 stores compressed detailed history, short-retention raw evidence, learned model snapshots/refined histories/backups as intended by production architecture.

title: Queue/DLQ asynchronous jobs
requirement: Heavy asynchronous evidence/Atlas/trust/smoothing/history work uses Queue/DLQ semantics so retries/duplicates cannot silently lose data.

title: Fast live current path
requirement: Accepted current fix reaches authoritative current state/WebSocket/map independently of slower history/Atlas/R2/geocode/backlog work.

title: Live-path instrumentation
requirement: Instrument source age, local persist, phone send, backend processing, WebSocket and browser render delay so live latency is measured rather than guessed.

title: Current state cannot roll back
requirement: Old/out-of-order/fallback/background results cannot overwrite newer authoritative measured/current device state.

title: Server ACK means durable acceptance
requirement: Backend sends ACK only after crossing the durability boundary the device cleanup/reconciliation contract relies on.

title: Backend idempotency
requirement: Duplicate at-least-once delivery is safe across device ingestion, Queue/DLQ jobs and safety events.

title: Public Worker input bounds
requirement: Device/browser/command/history APIs enforce explicit request size/complexity/time bounds and reject oversized/hostile inputs without uncontrolled work.

title: Cloud health/watchdog
requirement: Backend detects missing device heartbeat, queue/DLQ/database/provider problems and exposes useful degraded/offline health without one missed packet causing alert spam.

title: Retention lifecycle
requirement: Detailed raw/trusted/history/log/evidence/safety/audit retention follows explicit policy and automated cleanup cannot delete unrelated records.

title: Backup and restore
requirement: Critical configuration/history/index state has a backup strategy and destructive isolated restore test proves devices/history/config relationships actually recover.

title: Cloud secrets not public
requirement: Worker/provider credentials and production secrets stay in appropriate secret/binding storage and never enter source/client bundles/log output.

title: Deployment/migration ordering
requirement: Production deploy applies compatible schemas/migrations/bindings before traffic requires them and has a documented rollback/fail-safe strategy.

title: WebSocket reconnect semantics
requirement: Disconnect/reconnect restores newest current state then resumes pushes without duplicate/stale state poisoning.

title: Queue batching
requirement: High-frequency history/evidence work batches appropriately rather than forcing tiny expensive handler invocations while live path stays responsive.

title: OneMap token lifecycle
requirement: Backend manages authenticated OneMap token refresh-before-expiry with bounded retry and central limiting below provider ceiling; enrichment outage does not break Brick state.

title: Reverse-geocode coalescing/cache
requirement: Live 2-second tracking cadence does not create 2-second authenticated reverse-geocode calls; enrichment requests are cached/coalesced/async.

title: Exact deployment identity
requirement: Deployed backend/dashboard/schema/protocol/map/Atlas versions are recorded and match the production APK release record.

title: Permanent release signing identity
requirement: Production APK uses the permanent Brick V1 signing identity; private key/passwords remain outside Git and recovery material is securely backed up/tested.

title: Release APK not debug
requirement: Candidate is built with release configuration, non-debuggable production settings and reviewed R8/ProGuard/shrinker configuration.

title: APK hash/certificate recorded
requirement: Record APK SHA-256, versionCode/versionName, package and signing-certificate fingerprint for the exact candidate.

title: Final APK inspection
requirement: Inspect packaged manifest, permissions, exported components, package/version, certificate, network security, dependencies, services and receivers against audited source.

title: Source-to-artifact trace
requirement: Release metadata binds final APK to exact Android source/workflow/build configuration and proves no mystery/manual binary substitution.

title: Matching backend/browser deployment
requirement: Candidate APK is tested against exact recorded backend/browser/schema/protocol/map/Atlas revisions it expects.

title: GitHub signing secret hygiene
requirement: Raw keystore/private key/passwords are not committed; CI secret injection does not expose them in artifacts/logs.

title: CI/workflows green but not sufficient
requirement: Required build/lint/test/security workflows must pass, but green CI alone never grants production acceptance without device/integration criteria.

title: Schema/protocol release metadata
requirement: Release record explicitly captures database schema/migration and wire protocol versions and compatibility expectations.

title: Post-deploy smoke test
requirement: After exact deployment, run authenticated legitimate-parent and unauthenticated/wrong-client smoke/security checks before freezing release.

title: Release tag/freeze
requirement: After acceptance, tag/freeze exact source/deployment identities and preserve setup/recovery instructions so V1 remains reproducible.

title: No PRODUCTION QUALIFIED before Phase 9
requirement: Before complete real OPPO/endurance/production acceptance, classification is at most RELEASE CANDIDATE.

title: 72-hour untouched
requirement: Exact production candidate runs at least 72 hours untouched on required target device with tracking/journal/backend/health intact and zero manual recovery.

title: 7-day untouched
requirement: Exact production candidate runs seven days untouched with required continuity, data integrity, recovery and measured resource use.

title: Overnight screen-off
requirement: Screen-off overnight does not silently stop tracking/safety/journal and recovery does not require opening Brick.

title: Doze
requirement: Doze behavior is tested on real ColorOS target; required safety/durable behavior survives and expected cadence changes are honest.

title: Battery saver
requirement: Battery Saver test proves core safety/journal/tracking degrade safely without manual restart; optional work reduces first.

title: Low battery
requirement: Low/critical battery behavior records/alerts according to policy and does not corrupt pending data.

title: Charging
requirement: Charging transitions are captured and no lifecycle/power-policy bug appears when charging/unplugging.

title: Wi-Fi-cellular transitions
requirement: Repeated Wi-Fi <-> cellular handover keeps current state/journal/reconnect correct without duplicate/lost sequences.

title: Two-hour Internet outage
requirement: At least a two-hour complete Internet outage preserves local collection and later catch-up/reconciliation automatically.

title: Indoor degraded position
requirement: Real indoor/degraded GNSS environment exercises assisted/estimated/anchor/coarse/last-known/unknown transitions honestly.

title: GNSS loss/recovery
requirement: GNSS loss triggers legitimate fallback/reacquisition and later measured fix reconverges without raw/history corruption.

title: App process kill
requirement: Killing Brick app process exercises supported process/lifecycle recovery without manual app launch and without losing durable data.

title: Network-engine failure
requirement: Kill/fail Brick network engine and prove module-level automatic repair before whole-app escalation.

title: Cloudflare outage
requirement: Temporarily make production-like Cloudflare backend unreachable; phone queues safely and recovers/catches up automatically.

title: Duplicate packets
requirement: Inject duplicate telemetry/queue events and prove idempotent current/history/safety behavior.

title: Out-of-order packets
requirement: Inject out-of-order/gap traffic and prove current state never rolls back, gaps reconcile and history ordering remains correct.

title: Corrupt/malformed payload
requirement: Corrupted/invalid protocol input is rejected safely without backend/device crash or poisoning state.

title: Thousands/large queued records
requirement: Large backlog upload/reconciliation does not starve SOS/current state, corrupt journal, OOM, duplicate history or require manual intervention.

title: ColorOS memory pressure
requirement: Real target-device memory pressure/process reclaim exercises self-recovery and durable state restoration.

title: Phone reboot
requirement: Reboot restores required core state/tracking automatically through supported Android/managed lifecycle mechanisms.

title: App update
requirement: Upgrade from previous compatible candidate preserves pairing, key identity, durable journal, schema/state and resumes correctly.

title: Worker deployment during operation
requirement: Deploy/replace backend Worker during active device/portal operation and prove reconnect/compatibility/data integrity.

title: Location callback stall
requirement: Simulate/induce stale callback/subscription and prove bounded active reacquisition/repair occurs before fallback; no false permanent degraded state.

title: Old fallback race
requirement: Force old slow fallback result to complete after newer measured fix and prove it cannot overwrite current state.

title: Parent Location child override
requirement: Parent ON -> verify ON -> child OFF remains OFF; Parent OFF -> verify OFF -> child ON remains ON; no hidden enforcement loop.

title: Scheduled Wi-Fi child override
requirement: Scheduled OFF -> child enables remains ON; scheduled ON -> child disables remains OFF until another explicit/scheduled action.

title: Notification-noise qualification
requirement: Healthy tracking/Location control creates no separate/repeated noisy Brick GPS-on popup while required platform FGS/privacy disclosures remain visible.

title: Fast live path
requirement: Measure accepted-position -> parent-render pipeline stages on real candidate and prove slow history/Atlas/backlog/geocoding does not head-of-line block live state.

title: Backup destructive restore
requirement: Create backup, destroy/replace isolated test DB/state, restore fresh, and verify device/history/config/relationship integrity.

title: Provider crash isolation
requirement: Crash/fail Wi-Fi, BLE, magnetic, Atlas, particle and Shizuku enhancements independently and prove Brick Core tracking/safety continues.

title: Storage pressure/write death
requirement: Test low storage plus process death during journal/database write; protected unsent/safety data and database integrity survive or fail safely.
